decisions.reason: The peak-alignment decision applies only to the Hero V and É accent. The source message separately reports a second-V execution failure, which is already represented and is not a propagated effect of this source MODIFY.

The approved Hero V can remain the fixed reference geometry while the É accent is positioned to match its terminal peak; the source decision does not necessarily alter any intrinsic Hero V geometry attribute.
The source explicitly adds an exact peak-alignment rule between two forms governed by the shared signature terminal treatment.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Kenji,

We are exactly where we hoped to be: seeing the complete wordmark at last is exciting, confirms an important milestone, and makes the priorities for the next round much clearer. The Hero V has established the standard, so my attention has shifted away from it and toward bringing the remaining letters up to that same level.

The main issue is that the E and L currently speak a different visual language from the Hero V. Their small flared terminals recall the Roman-flare direction we deliberately left behind, so please redesign the Es and Ls to feel custom and architectural rather than as though they came from an existing typeface. The second V also needs some of its proprietary quality restored: in the isolated studies, the almost imperceptible extra reach of its right arm made it feel uniquely Veillvé, and I’d like that gesture carried back into the wordmark.

One refinement remains for the Hero V and É accent, even though both are moving in a very good direction. Please bring their highest terminal points to exactly the same height so the peaks align perfectly; if the accent is literally a slice of the Hero V, that alignment should be exact.

value_updates.hero_e_accent_peak_alignment: The highest terminal points of the Hero V and É accent must be exactly the same height.

decisions.reason: The peak-alignment decision does not change the E and L construction requirement. Their separate same-message redesign is already represented by the existing MODIFY.
Exact terminal-peak alignment is a geometry and positioning constraint and does not change the deferred champagne-gold material treatment.
The exact shared height of the opening Hero V and closing É accent adds a concrete alignment relationship within the complete wordmark composition.
